subject: On-prem attachment routing & control plane placement - Stedman POC
messages:
From: Seth Park <seth.park@stedman.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: cindy.lang@stedman.com, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Sep 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stedman POC - on-prem attachment routing question

Hi Lukas / Irene,

Thanks again for walking our infra team through the Redwood Private kit yesterday. Two items came up in our ops run-through that we want to resolve before the POC: control plane placement (customer VPC vs Redwood-managed control plane) and how the customer on-prem inference nodes will egress to external data stores without hairpinning through our control plane.

Current asks:
- Can we host the control plane components in our VPC while keeping the sensitive inference traffic strictly on our on-prem VLANs?
- For S3-like backup and observability egress, what routing options do you recommend (NAT at edge, egress proxy sidecars, or dedicated egress VMs)? We want to avoid double-bouncing (onprem -> Redwood controlplane -> internet).

I've attached our rough rack-level diagram (attachment-routing-v1.pdf) and an initial network sketch (controlplane-placement-diagram_v2.png).

Would appreciate a short write-up with recommended approaches + pros/cons. If useful, we can set a 30-min call next week.

Thanks,
Seth
Seth Park
SRE Lead, Stedman Logistics

From: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
To: Seth Park <seth.park@stedman.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Sep 2029 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stedman POC - on-prem attachment routing question

Seth — thanks for the clear ask and the diagrams, very helpful. High-level answers up front and then a short decision matrix below. Happy to sync Thursday if that works.

Short answers:
1) Control plane: We support two patterns for POC-grade deployments:
   - Customer-hosted control plane (recommended for regulated data): control plane services run inside Stedman VPC and are secured via VPC peering or PrivateLink to Redwood-managed sidecars.
   - Redwood-hosted control plane (operationally simpler): Redis/coordination remains in Redwood account; customer runs inference-only nodes that speak to a public-private endpoint with mTLS.

   Recommendation: For the POC, run control plane components in Stedman VPC (customer-hosted). It reduces egress of sensitive metadata and keeps audit boundaries clear.

2) Egress for artifacts/telemetry: Avoid hairpinning through our control plane. Options:
   - Edge NAT in customer DC: route outbound to the internet (S3 endpoints) directly via local NAT gateway. Minimal latency, simplest.
   - Egress proxy sidecars on inference nodes: allows fine-grained policy and observability, but adds CPU and complexity.
   - Dedicated egress VM pair that peers to the control plane for config but carries traffic directly to the internet (middle-ground).

Decision matrix (pros/cons):
- Customer NAT: simplest, least disruption, recommended for POC unless the customer requires per-request filtering/inspection.
- Sidecars: best when you need per-request auth, tagging, or central sampling control (adds Ops overhead).
- Dedicated egress VMs: good compromise for customers who want central control without sidecarization.

Action items if you choose customer-hosted control plane:
- We provide a small cloudformation/terraform artifact to spin up the control plane components (IAM roles, subnets, security groups).
- You'll need to expose private endpoints to the inference nodes (VPC peering or PrivateLink).
- Certificate exchange: we will provide CSR template and expect mTLS between inference agents and control plane endpoints.

I'll drop a short tech note and attach a diagram mapping that control-plane-in-customer-VPC flow.

— Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Stedman POC - on-prem attachment routing question

Putting a few operational considerations on the table from the ops/observability side: 

- If Stedman runs the control plane in their VPC, ensure the VPC has 2x AZ spread for control plane HA. We will need consistent RTT for our healthchecks.
- Telemetry / logs: prefer pushing logs to a customer-owned S3 or Splunk via direct peering; if they choose sidecars, include a metrics forwarder that tags token/account id.
- Egress ACLs: recommend a small managed egress ACL list from Redwood with required FQDNs and destination ranges to reduce firewall churn on day 0. We'll supply that list.

Minor note: for the POC, sidecars are probably overkill; customer NAT + one egress VM pair is pragmatic.

-- Irene
Irene Choi
Platform Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks Lukas / Irene — that helps a lot. We're leaning to the customer-hosted control plane + dedicated egress VMs approach for the POC. Two follow-ups:
1) Can you send the terraform snippet and the minimal SG/route table changes we need?
2) For certificate exchange, do you expect our KMS to sign or should we use Redwood-provided certs for the mTLS client certs?

Also, we booked Thu 09/19 11:00 PT for a short call to run through the diagram you've attached.

— Seth

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Cc: cindy.lang@stedman.com

Subject: Re: Stedman POC - on-prem attachment routing question

Seth — good decision for the POC. Quick answers for your follow-ups:
1) Terraform/snippet: attaching a minimal module (see related_links) that creates: private subnets for control plane, a pair of NAT instances (or managed NAT gateways), SGs allowing inbound mTLS on TCP 443 from inference node subnets, and route table entries for peering. We'll publish a github gist after the call.
2) Certs: For POC we can use Redwood-issued short-lived certs (automated rotation). For long-term/production you should use your KMS/HSM to sign a CA and we will accept it for mTLS mutual-auth. Steps:
   - POC: Redwood issues leaf cert; we manage rotation via our control plane agent.
   - Prod: you generate a customer CA in your KMS, provide the cert chain and trust bundle, and we'll configure agents to trust it.

Action: Lukas and I will post the terraform snippet + minimal ACL FQDN list to the Drive link before the Thu meeting.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Cloud Solutions, Redwood Inference
